binding.storage: control SQLite table shiyu_channel_conversation_bindings (channel_ref PK, conversation_id UNIQUE, scope, version, applied_invalidation_watermark, last invalidation metadata, timestamps) on the single SqliteTransactions connection
binding.creation: default target = ConversationStore.ensureConversation(from toConversationKey(channel audience, scope)), so the binding and the conversation are written in one transaction and repeated delivery/binding never creates a second conversation; an explicit existing conversationId may be supplied instead (must be owned, same scope, active)
binding.idempotency: same channelRef+conversation produces a stable duplicate result without version bump; concurrent duplicate binds still produce exactly one durable row
binding.cas: rebinding to another conversation requires expectedBindingVersion == current version; an older reader gets VERSION_CONFLICT and can never overwrite the newer binding; bindings without a version are refused (BINDING_VERSION_REQUIRED) and conversation_id is globally unique (BINDING_CONFLICT)
binding.refusals: forged channelRef (UNKNOWN_CHANNEL_CONVERSATION/INVALID_SCHEMA), revoked channel audience (CHANNEL_AUDIENCE_REVOKED), scope the owner cannot manage (UNAUTHORIZED_BINDING), binding-scope change (CROSS_SCOPE_BINDING), foreign/other-scope conversation (CROSS_SCOPE_BINDING), missing conversation (INVALID_CONVERSATION), archived conversation (INACTIVE_CONVERSATION), capacity 128 (BINDING_CAPACITY)
binding.restart: bindings, versions and applied invalidation watermarks are durable and survive a Worker restart (covered by the real Worker test); a restarted bind replays as duplicate with the same conversationId

invalidationBridge.sinkPath: IngressDomain.setInvalidationSink(signal => ConversationDomain.bridgeChannelInvalidation(...)) runs synchronously inside the accepting channel transaction; ConversationDomain calls ConversationStore.invalidateAudience (audienceVersion++, reply-binding sessionEpoch++/routingRevision++ in the same writer transaction); unbound channel conversations are a deliberate no-op
invalidationBridge.atomicity: a sink/bridge failure rolls the channel audience change (including its invalidation ledger and deletion watermark) together with the ConversationStore write back; this is proven by a real ConversationStore draft becoming STALE_CONTEXT after audience change/member removal/deletion and by an injected sink-failure rollback test
invalidationBridge.draftEffect: old drafts retire via ConversationStore token checks: assertDraftCurrent throws STALE_CONTEXT after an audience change, member removal and message deletion respectively; the binding projection exposes conversationAudienceVersion and replySessionEpoch so the Runtime can display the same fact
invalidationBridge.pullPath: ChannelRuntimeBridge.bridgePending() reads channel.invalidationsAfter and applies each still-pending signal to its bound conversation through conversation.channelInvalidate; per-binding applied_invalidation_watermark makes retries/host restarts idempotent (a second page/run applies 0 additional changes); unbound signals stay pending and are reported
invalidationBridge.lateBinding: invalidations emitted before a binding stay in the channel ledger; after binding, bridgePending() applies them (conservative whole-audience invalidation), so a restart/pending window cannot silently reuse a stale draft

projection.readOnly: three bounded reads only (channel.status, channel.snapshot, conversation.channelBindings + bounded invalidations page); 100 real Worker refreshes leave control commitSeq unchanged; no capture/creation/write
projection.lossless: plain JSON with no explicit undefined, NaN/Infinity/-0, sparse arrays, accessors or symbol keys; an independent lossless checker + JSON round-trip runs against the real Worker projection (required before embedding into a DSH tool/snapshot)
projection.honestDegraded: channel ingress unavailable or conversation domain unavailable produce status/degraded markers instead of empty success; bindings/pending/watermarks remain inspectable where their sources exist
projection.safety: no message bodies, summaries or body references in the projection; participants are reduced to counts; no authority/Mandate/credential is exposed

identityMapping.conversationKey: ChannelRuntimeBridge.conversationKey()/channelConversationKey() produce the exact existing ConversationKey {connectionId, platformConversationId:nativeConversationId, threadId?, kind:mode, scope}; the binding test proves the derived conversationId equals the ConversationStore.ensureConversation result for that key
identityMapping.innerAccount: channel.getParticipant().innerAccount is re-validated by channelParticipantAccount() against the H4 InnerAccount contract; the bridge registers it via relationship.registerSubject
identityMapping.noMerge: two accounts with identical short participant ids/message ids and identical display names produce distinct InnerAccount tuples and distinct relationship entityIds; the same tuple re-registers idempotently (created=false)
